eps.d: Young Mr. Grace has died and the Grace Brothers department store has closed. The former staff attend a reading of his will, and find they have inherited a hotel.
After their first night in their own hotel the former staff of Grace Brothers are settling into their new roles. However, they need money to get the hotel running.
Mrs. Slocombe finds herself in court for stealing a horse-drawn cart and Mr. Humphries' relationship with Mavis Moulterd continues to develop.
A party of Americans have come to stay at the Millstone Country Hotel for a weekend. It means £1,000 plus tips, so the staff set about bringing the ageing hotel up to scratch.

eps.t: Good Help is Hard to Find
eps.d: After the interviews for staff fail miserably, the former Grace Brothers team must work at their own hotel. In the night, a storm knocks out the electricity with scary results.
The former staff of Grace Brothers have now taken on their new roles as staff at the Millstone Country Hotel, but their having trouble settling in.
Mavis Moulterd has still got a mad, passionate crush on Mr. Humphries. Mrs. Slocombe gets a letter from an old friend and Captain Peacock finds a loaded gun in the writing room.
The staff continue the tradition of hosting and taking part in a cricket match. However, preparations don't go quite as smoothly as expected.

eps.t: Breaking Up is Hard to Do
eps.d: Mrs. Slocombe is stunned when her long lost husband appears to have made enquiries about buying the hotel. He's been missing since he went to a supermarket in 1942.
Captain Peacock discovers a dead cat hidden behind one of the walls. After they get rid of it, they find it was put in the hotel to cancel out bad luck.
Mr. Rumbold gets a vote of no confidence. It seems his wife has left him, which has made him more pompous. Meanwhile, the staff agree to play a darts match with the villagers.
A group of businessmen due to stay at the manor are expecting some culture-Shakespeare and opera. But with no money to spend on entertainment, there seems to be only one answer.
